newsitem.title: USA: U.S. economic conditions best in 30 years - Rubin.
newsitem.headline: U.S. economic conditions best in 30 years - Rubin.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin Thursday called U.S. economic conditions the best for 30 years.
But he told a forum sponsored by the John F. Kennedy School that more needed to be done to tackle poverty in the inner cities and elsewhere.

"Today, America is in the midst of sustained economic recovery," he said. "It has the best conditions we've seen in the last 30 years -- strong job creation, low unemployment, low interest rates, low inflation."
Rubin called the health of the inner cities critical to America's future.
"Far too many people are caught up in the cycle of poverty," he said.
He pledged that the Clinton administration would continue to fight for expanded government funding for a variety of programs aimed at alleviating poverty, including community development banks.
